pedagogical_insights.false_positive_explanation: A False Positive (FP=3) occurs when a legitimate message (HAM) is incorrectly classified as SPAM. In real-world SMS filtering, high FP is dangerous because users may miss critical two-factor authentication (2FA) OTP codes, banking alerts, flight notifications, or emergency personal messages.
pedagogical_insights.false_negative_explanation: A False Negative (FN=14) occurs when an unwanted or malicious message (SPAM) is mistakenly classified as legitimate (HAM). While less catastrophic than losing a genuine message, a high FN rate exposes the user to fraudulent phishing links, financial scams, and nuisance advertising.
